newsitem.title: POLAND: Confused storks turn back from Poland to Africa.
newsitem.headline: Confused storks turn back from Poland to Africa.

text.p: Some of the storks flying north to nest in Poland have been turning back towards Africa because of confusing weather, Polish public television said on Tuesday.
It quoted ornithologists as saying such behaviour during the annual migration had not been observed for a century.
"The cause of the storks' strange behaviour is changes in the European climate," the television said.

"For several weeks the birds, waiting for warmer weather, have been circling above Turkey and the Balkans and many have fallen due to lack of food," it reported, adding that some were expected to start reaching Poland soon but would be exhausted.
About 15,000 pairs of storks nest in Poland, which is summer home to a quarter of the world's total population of the large, long-beaked and spindly-legged birds.
But spring came late to Poland this year and half of the nests in the Mazurian lakes district and in central Pomerania, along the Baltic coast, have yet to be reclaimed by their owners.
The storks' actions this spring were discovered thanks to satellite transmitters fitted to rings on the birds by German ornithologists, the television reported.
Storks are loved in Poland as symbols of spring, for bringing luck and for their picturesque, unruly nests often perched on chimney stacks.
